patch.summary:
Choose Apify only if your buying job matches “Actor platform for web scraping — Free $0 ($5 usage); Starter $29/mo ($26 annual); Scale $” rather than incident.io's shape. Choose incident.io only if your buying job matches “Incident response — Basic Free; Team $15/user/mo annual ($19 monthly); Pro $25/user; on-ca” rather than Apify's shape. Workflow advantage: Apify leans web-data-collection; incident.io leans incident-oncall. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Positioning: Apify is Actor platform for web scraping — Free $0 ($5 usage); Starter $29/mo ($26 annual); Scale $199; Business $999.; incident.io is Incident response — Basic Free; Team $15/user/mo annual ($19 monthly); Pro $25/user; on-call add-on +$10–$20/user. Does not outrank PagerDut.
- Company-size focus: Apify (solo, micro, small-business) vs incident.io (small-business, mid-market).
- Workflow coverage skew: Apify-leaning web-data-collection vs incident.io-leaning incident-oncall.
- Researched limits: Apify — Prepaid usage does not roll over — unused credits expire each cycle; incident.io — On-call paging is an add-on (+$10–$20/user), not included in the $15 Team floor.

Limitations — Apify: Prepaid usage does not roll over — unused credits expire each cycle; Actor Store and proxy GB costs can exceed the plan sticker quickly; incident.io: On-call paging is an add-on (+$10–$20/user), not included in the $15 Team floor; Does not outrank PagerDuty (8.0) as the incident-oncall award.
